newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kornblum sees Draskovic, backs "democratic process".
newsitem.headline: Kornblum sees Draskovic, backs "democratic process".

text.p: A top U.S. envoy on the former Yugoslavia spent more than two hours in talks with Serbian opposition leader Vuk Draskovic on Sunday and afterwards expressed support for the "democratic process" in Serbia.

Draskovic told reporters after his meeting with U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum that the Dayton peace accord was in danger. Draskovic, who heads the Serb Renewal Movement, said the opposition was seeking "diplomatic support" from the U.S. government as well as member countries of the European Union.
Kornblum also met Vojin Dimitrijovic of the Civic Alliance and Ivan Vujacic of the Democratic Party, at a Geneva hotel. He is in the Swiss city to attend a humanitarian meeting on Monday.

Kornblum, referring to President Slobodan Milosevic's cancelling of opposition victories in local elections last month, told reporters: "We believe it is now essential for Mr. Milosevic to accept the result of the election and open himself to continuing the democratic process and particularly to allow much greater freedom of the media."

"We will continue our support of the democratic processes there and expect that (the same) of Milosevic really as the price for any further movement in relations...That is a very strong position which gives Milosevic a clear signal of our support for the democratic process," he added.

Draskovic said Milosevic had provoked "violence, bloodshed and even civil war in Serbia", adding: "The Dayton agreement is in danger. Mr. Milosevic must be stopped. Mr. Milosevic must start to think in a democratic way first of all and recognise the election will of the people."
